metadata.title: Product Bricks & Streams
metadata.description: Hierarchical product brick map for the paramedical-and-mental-health-practice-platform domain, modeled on Health Cloud Initiative (HCI): the paramedical practice management and EPD of FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, ParaNICE and HCI One (agenda and online booking, dossier and care pathways, voice-to-text, measurements, GDS801 declarations through Vecozo, patient invoicing with Mollie, billing services, dashboards and LDF quality delivery), the HCI CRS mental health care EPD (treatment plans, medication, ROM, client portal, zorgprestatiemodel and municipal contracting), the Uw Zorg Online and Quli patient environments, Embloom, Emogy and NICE Connect e-health and remote care, the ZorgDomein, ZorgMail, HIS/AIS and partner API integrations with practice websites and the Zorgverlener App, and the platform foundation of identity (UZI/DigiD), audit and consent, multi-tenant runtime with label migration tooling and customer support.

rootGroups.name: Paramedical Practice Management and EPD
rootGroups.description: The practice management system and electronic patient record for physiotherapy, exercise therapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, dietetics, podiatry and rehabilitation care: the agenda and online booking, the web-based dossier with care pathways, voice-to-text and measurements, declarations through Vecozo with patient invoicing and billing services, and the dashboards and quality-register deliveries that FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry and ParaNICE bring together in HCI One.

subGroups.name: Scheduling and Booking
subGroups.description: The agenda as the central heart of the practice, 24/7 online booking with waiting list and reminders, and group lessons, programmes and subscriptions.

bricks.name: Agenda and Multi-location Scheduling
bricks.description: The agenda that FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura and HCI One all describe as the central heart of the practice: one calendar per therapist and per treatment room across every location, with treatment codes, referral and episode linked to each appointment so that the dossier opens with one click and the declaration is generated from the agenda rather than typed again. It handles recurring series, waiting-room check-in, no-shows and moves between therapists, and it is the timeline that group lessons, online booking, patient self-service, the Zorgverlener App and the BI dashboards all read from. In HCI One the agenda is the first component shared by every discipline, so its slot model must carry physiotherapy, speech therapy, dietetics and GGZ session types alike.

bricks.name: Online Booking, Waiting List and Reminders
bricks.description: The 24/7 online booking that SpotOnMedics made its calling card and that HCI One carries forward: a booking widget on the practice website and in the Uw Zorg Online app that shows real free slots from the agenda, lets new and existing patients choose a therapist, location and treatment type, and confirms the appointment directly in the practice agenda. It also runs the waiting list that fills cancellations automatically and the SMS, e-mail and push reminders that reduce no-shows. Raising the online booking share is one of the year-one levers for administrative relief, because every self-booked appointment is a phone call the front desk does not take.

bricks.name: Group Lessons, Programmes and Subscriptions
bricks.description: Group management as SpotOnMedics markets it, carried forward in HCI One for practices that also run medical fitness, fall prevention, COPD and back-school groups, running programmes and subscriptions next to insured treatment: defining a lesson or programme, its capacity and trainers, enrolling participants, tracking attendance and billing the participant per session, per period or by direct debit. Because these services are usually uninsured, the brick sits between the agenda and patient invoicing rather than the declaration engine, and it is the part of the platform that turns a physiotherapy practice into a health centre with recurring revenue.

bricks.name: Patient Dossier and Care Pathways
bricks.description: The web-based electronic patient record that is the FysioRoadmap foundation of HCI One: the patient's profile and referral, treatment episodes with intake, examination, diagnosis, goals, treatment plan, evaluations and discharge, structured as customisable care pathways per discipline so that a physiotherapist, speech therapist, dietitian and podiatrist each see their own workflow on the same record. It stores clinical notes, documents and correspondence, enforces dossier completeness rules that insurers and quality audits check, and exposes the episode data that declarations, quality delivery and dashboards derive from. Consolidating eight labels into this one dossier model, with phased per-discipline migration and no forced deadline, is the core of the HCI One programme.

bricks.name: Clinical Guidelines and Discipline Templates

Practices can extend templates with their own protocols, and the specialisation cards that SpotOnMedics markets are one packaging of this content. In HCI One, this brick is what allows one dossier to serve eight labels' disciplines.

bricks.name: Voice-to-Text and AI Documentation
bricks.description: The SmartAI voice-to-text that HCI CRS ships for GGZ and the dictation and AI summarisation HCI is rolling out across the paramedical labels: a therapist dictates during or right after a consultation, the transcript is structured into the fields of the active pathway step or treatment plan, and the therapist reviews, edits and signs the draft before it becomes part of the dossier. Every draft records which model produced it and that a professional accepted it, audio is discarded after transcription unless the practice opts to keep it, and processing stays with EU-hosted providers under a processing agreement. It is the most direct answer to the working day per week that physiotherapists report spending on administration.

bricks.name: Declaration Engine (GDS801 and Zorgprestatiemodel)
bricks.description: The engine that turns registered treatments into insurer claims without retyping: for paramedical care it composes GDS801 declarations (the standard that replaced PM304 on 1 January 2025) from the agenda and episode, checks the referral, insurance coverage, treatment count and diagnosis codes against the insurer's contract and the patient's policy, and for GGZ it builds zorgprestatiemodel claims per consult, setting and profession, carrying the referral date that is mandatory on every declaration from 2026. Claims are batched per insurer, submitted through the Vecozo gateway and reconciled with return messages, and every rejected line becomes a correction task instead of lost revenue. With more than €500 million in annual declarations reported by 2022, this is the brick where a standard change without a rejection spike is a strategic objective.
